To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the GEOS-5 AGCM is updated to include the effects of cool-skin and diurnal warming on Ts; 2) the GEOS atmospheric data analysis system is updated to assimilate AVHRR radiance observations; and 3) the GEOS data analysis system is able to assimilate AVHR radiance observations more effectively when Ts is modified.

assimilation of SST-relevant AVHRR radiances in the GEOS-5 ADAS improves the fit to withheld in situ SST observations and improves the fit to radiance measurements from the AIRS and IASI hyperspectral sensors.
assimilation of SST-relevant satellite IR observations in GEOS-5 ADAS improves the fit to withheld, near-surface in-situ buoy SST measurements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the assimilation of IR observations in the presence of a diurnal cycle in the ocean surface temperature.
the development of an oceanic data assimilation system in GEOS-5, and the results of this study are a step in that direction.
the development and evaluation of a new SST assimilation scheme for GEOS-ADAs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ts modification is a necessary and important step towards a fully-coupled atmosphere-ocean data assimilation system.
the assimilated Ts in GEOS-5 ADAS is an improved representation of the actual SST, and this improvement is beneficial in the context of the GEOS-5 data assimilation system.
assimilation of SST-relevant IR observations in GEOS-5 ADAS, using a Ts that accounts for near surface effects, is beneficial.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the assimilation of IR observations of Ts in GEOS-5 is feasible.
the Ts modification is a step towards an integrated atmosphere-ocean data assimilation system.
the Ts assimilation is a step in the right direction for the development of a GEOS atmosphere-ocean coupled DA system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GEOS atmospheric model can be used to assimilate SST-relevance satellite radiance observations.
the Ts assimilation in the GEOS system is a step towards the development of a coupled atmosphere-ocean system.
assimilating Ts in a coupled data assimilation context is a nontrivial task and requires careful tuning of the atmospheric model.
